claim: In fission yeast, the ste11 gene encodes the master regulator initiating the switch from vegetative growth to gametogenesis.
source: In fission yeast, the ste11 gene encodes the master regulator initiating the switch from vegetative growth to gametogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript (Anandhakumar et al., 2013).

claim: Methylation of H3K4 and consequent promoter nucleosome deacetylation repress ste11 induction and cell differentiation.
source: In a previous paper, we showed that the methylation of H3K4 and consequent promoter nucleosome deacetylation repress ste11 induction and cell differentiation (Materne et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: H2B deubiquitylation and the RSC remodeling complex are activators of ste11 expression.
source: Here we report a genetic screen that highlighted H2B deubiquitylation and the RSC remodeling complex as activators of ste11 expression.
evidence: This claim is based on the genetic screen results presented in the manuscript.

claim: H2Bubi has opposite roles at the promoter where it represses expression, and over the transcribed region where it sustains it.
source: Mechanistic analyses revealed more complex, opposite roles of H2Bubi at the promoter where it represses expression, and over the transcribed region where it sustains it.
evidence: This claim is supported by mechanistic analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: H2Bubi promotes H3K4 methylation at the promoter.
source: By promoting H3K4 methylation at the promoter, H2Bubi initiates the deacetylation process, which decreases chromatin remodeling by RSC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing the relationship between H2Bubi and H3K4me3.

claim: H2Bubi initiates the deacetylation process, which decreases chromatin remodeling by RSC.
source: By promoting H3K4 methylation at the promoter, H2Bubi initiates the deacetylation process, which decreases chromatin remodeling by RSC.
evidence: This claim is supported by mechanistic data linking H2Bubi to deacetylation and RSC recruitment.

claim: Upon induction, efficient NDR (nucleosome depleted region) formation leads to high expression of ste11.
source: Upon induction, this process is reversed and efficient NDR (nucleosome depleted region) formation leads to high expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by nucleosome occupancy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: H2Bubi represses gametogenesis by opposing the recruitment of RSC at the promoter of the master regulator ste11 gene.
source: Therefore, H2Bubi represses gametogenesis by opposing the recruitment of RSC at the promoter of the master regulator ste11 gene.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: The RNA polymerase II (PolII) subunit Rpb1 C-terminal Domain shows a stereotypical pattern of CTD phosphorylation with phospho-S5 (S5P) peaking near the transcription start site (TSS) and phospho-S2 (S2P) accumulating towards the 3'-end of the transcribed region.
source: The RNA polymerase II (PolII) subunit Rpb1 C-terminal Domain shows a stereotypical pattern of CTD phosphorylation with phospho-S5 (S5P) peaking near the transcription start site (TSS) and phospho-S2 (S2P) accumulating towards the 3'-end of the transcribed region (Buratowski, 2009; Cassart et al., 2012; Drogat and Hermand, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to established literature.

claim: The distribution of histone H3 lysine 4 methylation (H3K4me) mirrors S5P due to the direct recruitment of the H3 methyltransferase Set1-COMPASS by the S5P of PolII.
source: The distribution of histone H3 lysine 4 methylation (H3K4me) mirrors S5P due to the direct recruitment of the H3 methyltransferase Set1-COMPASS by the S5P of PolII (Keogh et al., 2005; Ng et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: In budding yeast, Set1 is the only H3K4 methyltransferase.
source: In budding yeast, Set1 is the only H3K4 methyltransferase and plays a repressive role on PHO5, PHO84 and GAL1 expression, suggesting that H3K4me creates a repressive chromatin configuration (Carvin and Kladde, 2004; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Set1 plays a repressive role on PHO5, PHO84 and GAL1 expression in budding yeast.
source: In budding yeast, Set1 is the only H3K4 methyltransferase and plays a repressive role on PHO5, PHO84 and GAL1 expression, suggesting that H3K4me creates a repressive chromatin configuration (Carvin and Kladde, 2004; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: H3K4me creates a repressive chromatin configuration.
source: In budding yeast, Set1 is the only H3K4 methyltransferase and plays a repressive role on PHO5, PHO84 and GAL1 expression, suggesting that H3K4me creates a repressive chromatin configuration (Carvin and Kladde, 2004; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is suggested based on the repressive role of Set1 on specific genes.

claim: Most genes are upregulated in fission yeast when Set1 is absent.
source: Most genes are also upregulated in fission yeast when Set1 is absent (Lorenz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The PHD finger protein Set3, which is part of the SET3C HDAC complex, binds H3K4me2 to mediate deacetylation of histones in the 5' regions.
source: The PHD finger protein Set3, which is part of the SET3C HDAC complex, binds H3K4me2 to mediate deacetylation of histones in the 5' regions (Kim and Buratowski, 2009; Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The PHD domain of the HDAC-associated ING2 protein mediates its binding to the di- and trimethylated H3K4 at the promoters of proliferation genes.
source: Similarly, the PHD domain of the HDAC-associated ING2 protein mediates its binding to the di- and trimethylated H3K4 at the promoters of proliferation genes (Pena et al., 2006; Shi et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Histone H2B is monoubiquitylated (H2Bubi) on the conserved lysine 119 in fission yeast.
source: Histone H2B is monoubiquitylated (H2Bubi) on the conserved lysine 119 in fission yeast.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about H2B ubiquitylation in fission yeast.

claim: In yeast, Rad6 and Bre1 function as conjugating enzyme (E2) or ligase (E3) for H2B ubiquitylation.
source: In yeast, Rad6 and Bre1 function as conjugating enzyme (E2) or ligase (E3) (Hwang et al., 2003; Robzyk et al., 2000; Wood et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The H2B ubiquitylation pathway is conserved in fission yeast with the Rhp6 E2 and two Bre1 homologues, Brl1 and Brl2.
source: The pathway is conserved in fission yeast with the Rhp6 E2 and two Bre1 homologues, Brl1 and Brl2, a situation closer to higher eukaryotes (Tanny et al., 2007; Zofall and Grewal, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The presence of the Ubp8 deubiquitylase, which is part of the SAGA co-activator complex, underlies the dynamic nature of H2Bubi.
source: The presence of the Ubp8 deubiquitylase, which is part of the SAGA co-activator complex, underlies the dynamic nature of H2Bubi (Daniel et al., 2004; Henry et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: A second deubiquitylase, Ubp10, modulates the pool of H2Bubi.
source: A second deubiquitylase, Ubp10, modulates the pool of H2Bubi (Emre et al., 2005; Gardner et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: H2Bubi functions in a trans-tail regulation of H3K4 and H3K79 methylation.
source: H2Bubi functions in a trans-tail regulation of H3K4 and H3K79 methylation (Briggs et al., 2002; Dover et al., 2002; Ng et al., 2002; Sun and Allis, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The Set1-COMPASS subunit Swd2 is required for the crosstalk between H2Bubi and H3K4 methylation.
source: The Set1-COMPASS subunit Swd2 is required for the crosstalk by mechanisms implying its direct ubiquitylation by Rad6-Bre1 (Vitaliano-Prunier et al., 2008) or its recruitment by H2B-ub1 (Lee et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: H2Bubi is spread uniformly across transcribed units and at promoters.
source: H2Bubi is spread uniformly across transcribed units and at promoters (Batta et al., 2011; Schulze et al., 2011; 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Ubp8 acts at the 5' region where H3K4me3 is also high while Ubp10 targets the H3K79me3 decorated nucleosomes more typical of 3' regions.
source: Ubp8 acts at the 5' region where H3K4me3 is also high while Ubp10 targets the H3K79me3 decorated nucleosomes more typical of 3' regions, which suggests different, maybe opposite, roles of H2Bubi over the length of genes and spatial regulation (Schulze et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: H2Bubi plays a role in promoting nucleosome assembly leading to repression at promoters.
source: Nucleosome occupancy (Batta et al., 2011) in a strain lacking H2Bubi revealed a role in promoting nucleosome assembly leading to repression at promoters and a positive role during elongation by facilitating the eviction of the H2A-H2B dimer and nucleosome reassembly following the passage of the polymerase.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: H2Bubi plays a positive role during elongation by facilitating the eviction of the H2A-H2B dimer and nucleosome reassembly following the passage of the polymerase.
source: Nucleosome occupancy (Batta et al., 2011) in a strain lacking H2Bubi revealed a role in promoting nucleosome assembly leading to repression at promoters and a positive role during elongation by facilitating the eviction of the H2A-H2B dimer and nucleosome reassembly following the passage of the polymerase.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: RSC is ten-fold more abundant than the SWI/SNF complex and is essential for viability.
source: From the SWI/SNF-class remodeling complexes, RSC is ten-fold more abundant and is essential for viability, in contrast the SWI/SNF complex (Cairns et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: RSC is required for promoter nucleosome location.
source: RSC is required for promoter nucleosome location (Hartley and Madhani, 2009), consistent with its ability to slide nucleosomes in vitro (Lorch et al., 2011) and its global requirement for RNA polymerase II transcription (Parnell et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: RSC has the ability to slide nucleosomes in vitro.
source: RSC is required for promoter nucleosome location (Hartley and Madhani, 2009), consistent with its ability to slide nucleosomes in vitro (Lorch et al., 2011) and its global requirement for RNA polymerase II transcription (Parnell et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: RSC has a global requirement for RNA polymerase II transcription.
source: RSC is required for promoter nucleosome location (Hartley and Madhani, 2009), consistent with its ability to slide nucleosomes in vitro (Lorch et al., 2011) and its global requirement for RNA polymerase II transcription (Parnell et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: RSC recognizes acetylated nucleosomes through tandem bromodomains.
source: RSC recognizes acetylated nucleosomes through tandem bromodomains (Carey et al., 2006; Kasten et al., 2004), which links its recruitment to acetylation of histone H3 lysine 14.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: RSC recruitment is linked to acetylation of histone H3 lysine 14.
source: RSC recognizes acetylated nucleosomes through tandem bromodomains (Carey et al., 2006; Kasten et al., 2004), which links its recruitment to acetylation of histone H3 lysine 14.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that RSC recognizes acetylated nucleosomes through bromodomains.

claim: Promoter histone H2B ubiquitylation represses the expression of the master regulator of gametogenesis Ste11 in fission yeast.
source: Here we show that promoter H2B ubiquitylation represses the expression of the master regulator of gametogenesis Ste11 in fission yeast (Anandhakumar et al., 2013) by promoting Set1/H3K4me dependent deacetylation, which impedes the recruitment of the RSC complex.
evidence: This is the main finding of the manuscript, supported by experimental data.

claim: Promoter H2B ubiquitylation promotes Set1/H3K4me dependent deacetylation.
source: Here we show that promoter H2B ubiquitylation represses the expression of the master regulator of gametogenesis Ste11 in fission yeast (Anandhakumar et al., 2013) by promoting Set1/H3K4me dependent deacetylation, which impedes the recruitment of the RSC complex.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing the relationship between H2Bubi, H3K4me, and deacetylation.

claim: Set1/H3K4me dependent deacetylation impedes the recruitment of the RSC complex.
source: Here we show that promoter H2B ubiquitylation represses the expression of the master regulator of gametogenesis Ste11 in fission yeast (Anandhakumar et al., 2013) by promoting Set1/H3K4me dependent deacetylation, which impedes the recruitment of the RSC complex.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data showing reduced RSC occupancy when deacetylation is promoted.

claim: A H2B K119R mutant results in decreased nucleosome occupancy at the ste11 promoter and derepression of the gene.
source: A H2B K119R mutant results in decreased nucleosome occupancy at the ste11 promoter and derepression of the gene, while the absence of RSC has the opposite effect.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP and RT-Q-PCR data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The absence of RSC results in increased nucleosome occupancy at the ste11 promoter and repression of the gene.
source: A H2B K119R mutant results in decreased nucleosome occupancy at the ste11 promoter and derepression of the gene, while the absence of RSC has the opposite effect.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP and RT-Q-PCR data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The opposing role of promoter histone H2B ubiquitylation and RSC-dependent chromatin remodeling controls gametogenesis in fission yeast.
source: Therefore, the opposing role of promoter histone H2B ubiquitylation and RSC-dependent chromatin remodeling controls gametogenesis in fission yeast.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: The CTD S2 kinase Lsk1 is required for the completion of cytokinesis in response to perturbation of the actomyosin ring by latrunculin A (LatA).
source: In fission yeast, the CTD S2 kinase Lsk1 (latrunculin sensitive kinase - Cdk12 in higher eukaryotes) is required for the completion of cytokinesis in response to perturbation of the actomyosin ring by latrunculin A (LatA) (Karagiannis et al., 2005), and the deletion of lsk1 results in sensitivity to LatA.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: The deletion of lsk1 results in sensitivity to LatA.
source: In fission yeast, the CTD S2 kinase Lsk1 (latrunculin sensitive kinase - Cdk12 in higher eukaryotes) is required for the completion of cytokinesis in response to perturbation of the actomyosin ring by latrunculin A (LatA) (Karagiannis et al., 2005), and the deletion of lsk1 results in sensitivity to LatA.
evidence: This is a known phenotype of the lsk1 deletion mutant.

claim: The essential SIN (Septation Initiation Network) component encoding gene cdc14 is a potential transcriptional target of Lsk1.
source: Testing the LatA sensitivity of the genes we have previously identified (Coudreuse et al., 2010) as downregulated in a S2A mutant identified the essential SIN (Septation Initiation Network) component encoding gene cdc14 (Fankhauser and Simanis, 1993) as a potential transcriptional target of Lsk1.
evidence: This is inferred from the LatA sensitivity test and previous data on downregulated genes.

claim: The overexpression of cdc14 significantly suppresses the LatA sensitivity of a strain deleted for lsk1.
source: The overexpression of cdc14 significantly suppresses the LatA sensitivity of a strain deleted for lsk1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B), supporting that the LatA sensitivity of the lsk1 mutant relates to the downregulation of cdc14.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The LatA sensitivity of the lsk1 mutant relates to the downregulation of cdc14.
source: The overexpression of cdc14 significantly suppresses the LatA sensitivity of a strain deleted for lsk1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B), supporting that the LatA sensitivity of the lsk1 mutant relates to the downregulation of cdc14.
evidence: This is inferred from the suppression of LatA sensitivity by cdc14 overexpression.

claim: The screening for LatA sensitivity identified the SAGA-associated Ubp8 H2B ubiquitin protease and several components of the RSC and SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes.
source: The screening appeared to be consistent as the three kinases (Pmk1, Pek1 and Mkh1) forming the MAPK cell integrity transduction pathway were isolated. In addition, we identified the SAGA-associated Ubp8 H2B ubiquitin protease and several components of the RSC and SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complexes.
evidence: This is based on the results of the LatA sensitivity screen.

claim: The htb1 K119R mutant completely suppressed the lsk1 sensitivity to LatA.
source: Surprisingly, the htb1 K119R mutant completely suppressed the lsk1 sensitivity to the drug (Figure 1A), contrary to the deletion of ubp8.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The deletion of ubp8 did not suppress the lsk1 sensitivity to LatA.
source: Surprisingly, the htb1 K119R mutant completely suppressed the lsk1 sensitivity to the drug (Figure 1A), contrary to the deletion of ubp8.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The decrease in the level of the cdc14 mRNA observed in the lsk1 mutant was suppressed when H2Bubi was abolished in the htb1 K119R mutant.
source: The decrease in the level of the cdc14 mRNA observed in the lsk1 mutant was indeed suppressed when H2Bubi was abolished in the htb1 K119R mutant while the ubp8 mutant had no effect (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The ubp8 mutant had no effect on the level of cdc14 mRNA in the lsk1 mutant background.
source: The decrease in the level of the cdc14 mRNA observed in the lsk1 mutant was indeed suppressed when H2Bubi was abolished in the htb1 K119R mutant while the ubp8 mutant had no effect (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The ste11 gene is a key target of S2P.
source: The ste11 gene is another key target of S2P (Coudreuse et al., 2010; Materne et al., 2015; Schwer et al., 2012; Sukegawa et al., 2011), which is unrelated to LatA sensitivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to established literature.

claim: Lsk1 and S2P are critical regulators of the induction of gametogenesis by Ste11 by releasing Set1/H3K4me repression at the ste11 locus.
source: Lsk1 and S2P are critical regulators of the induction of gametogenesis by Ste11 by releasing Set1/H3K4me repression at the ste11 locus (Materne et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: The abolition of H2Bubi led to an increase of ste11 expression, including at the basal, non-induced state.
source: Similarly to cdc14, we observed that the abolition of H2Bubi led to an increase of ste11, including at the basal, non-induced state, supporting that ubiquitylation of H2B represses ste11 expression (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ubiquitylation of H2B represses ste11 expression.
source: Similarly to cdc14, we observed that the abolition of H2Bubi led to an increase of ste11, including at the basal, non-induced state, supporting that ubiquitylation of H2B represses ste11 expression (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is inferred from the increased ste11 expression when H2Bubi is abolished.

claim: An rhp6 deletion mutant (lacking the E2 ubiquitin conjugating enzyme) behaved similarly to the htb1 K119R mutant in terms of ste11 expression.
source: This was clearly an effect of the absence of ubiquitin on H2B as an rhp6 deletion mutant (lacking the E2 ubiquitin conjugating enzyme) behaved similarly (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The ubp8 deletion resulted in an increased level of ste11.
source: Paradoxically, the ubp8 deletion behaved similarly to the htb1 K119R mutant, also resulting in an increased level of ste11 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Either the absence, or the constitutive presence of ubiquitin on H2B results in the derepression of ste11.
source: Therefore, either the absence, or the constitutive presence of ubiquitin on H2B results in the derepression of ste11.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both htb1 K119R and ubp8 deletion lead to increased ste11 expression.

claim: Only the htb1 K119R mutant suppressed the defect of ste11 expression manifested in the lsk1 deletion strain.
source: However, only the htb1 K119R mutant suppressed the defect of expression manifested in the lsk1 deletion strain, in a way reminiscent of the cdc14 case (Figure 1C), which was confirmed by a phenotype assay (exposure to iodine that highlights gametogenesis by staining the gametes dark) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1C and phenotype assay shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The essential function of Lsk1 (namely S2P) for cdc14 or ste11 expression is not required when H2B cannot be ubiquitylated.
source: These genetic data suggest that the essential function of Lsk1 (namely S2P) for cdc14 or ste11 expression is not required when H2B cannot be ubiquitylated.
evidence: This is inferred from the suppression of lsk1 phenotypes by the htb1 K119R mutation.

claim: Lsk1 function is required for ubp8 to upregulate ste11 expression.
source: Contrary, Lsk1 function is required for ubp8 to upregulate ste11 expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the double lsk1 ubp8 mutant behaves as the single lsk1 mutant.

claim: A new monoclonal antibody specifically recognized the ubiquitylated version of H2B in fission yeast.
source: We tested the specificity of a new monoclonal antibody in fission yeast to avoid the caveats of using a tagged version. Despite two amino acid changes in the predicted epitope (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), the antibody specifically recognized the ubiquitylated version of H2B as no signal was observed in a K119R mutant (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The H2Bubi signal appeared increased in the ubp8 deletion strain.
source: The H2Bubi signal appeared increased in the ubp8 deletion strain but not in the absence of ubp16 that encodes the closest fission yeast orthologue to ScUBP10 (Kouranti et al., 2010; Sadeghi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The H2Bubi signal was not increased in the absence of ubp16.
source: The H2Bubi signal appeared increased in the ubp8 deletion strain but not in the absence of ubp16 that encodes the closest fission yeast orthologue to ScUBP10 (Kouranti et al., 2010; Sadeghi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The double ubp8 ubp16 mutant had similar level of H2Bubi to the single ubp8 mutant.
source: The double ubp8 ubp16 mutant had similar level of H2Bubi to the single ubp8 mutant, suggesting that Ubp8 is the genuine H2B deubiquitylase in fission yeast as previously proposed (Sadeghi et al., 2014) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Ubp8 is the genuine H2B deubiquitylase in fission yeast.
source: The double ubp8 ubp16 mutant had similar level of H2Bubi to the single ubp8 mutant, suggesting that Ubp8 is the genuine H2B deubiquitylase in fission yeast as previously proposed (Sadeghi et al., 2014) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ubp16 deletion does not affect H2Bubi levels and is supported by a citation.

claim: H2Bubi occupancy decreases at the ste11 promoter during gene induction.
source: A reverse pattern was observed at the promoter and 3'-distal region with H2Bubi occupancy decreasing at the promoter and increasing along the transcribed unit during gene induction (Figure 1E, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 1E, left panel.

claim: H2Bubi occupancy increases along the transcribed unit of ste11 during gene induction.
source: A reverse pattern was observed at the promoter and 3'-distal region with H2Bubi occupancy decreasing at the promoter and increasing along the transcribed unit during gene induction (Figure 1E, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 1E, left panel.

claim: H3K4me3 behaved similarly to H2Bubi at the ste11 promoter but was very low in the 3' region of ste11.
source: Considering the dependency of H3K4me to H2Bubi, we also followed the trimethyl mark (H3K4me3) that behaved similarly to H2Bubi at the promoter but was very low in the 3' region of ste11 (Figure 1E, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 1E, right panel.

claim: The deposition of H3K4me3 requires previous H2B ubiquitylation.
source: Therefore, the use of the htb1 K119R mutant confirmed that the deposition of H3K4me3 requires previous H2B ubiquitylation (Figure 1E, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 1E, right panel.

claim: The ubiquitylation of H2B represses transcription at the ste11 promoter while it promotes it during elongation.
source: We reasoned that the opposite dynamic of H2Bubi at the promoter and 3' region could reflect that the ubiquitylation represses transcription at the promoter while it promotes it during elongation, which could explain why both the htb1 K119R and the ubp8 deletion mutant lead to increased expression of ste11.
evidence: This is inferred from the opposite dynamics of H2Bubi at the promoter and 3' region.

claim: H3K4me3 represses ste11 expression by recruiting the SET3C HDAC, which is counteracted by Lsk1-dependent S2P.
source: In addition, our recent work indicated that H3K4me3 represses ste11 expression by recruiting the SET3C HDAC, which is counteracted by Lsk1-dependent S2P (Materne et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: In the htb1 K119R strain where H3K4me3 is downregulated, Lsk1 and S2P would not be required.
source: Therefore, in the htb1 K119R strain where H3K4me3 is downregulated (Figure 1E, right panel), Lsk1 and S2P would not be required, which is what we observe both genetically (Figure 1D) and by RT-Q-PCR (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is inferred from the downregulation of H3K4me3 in the htb1 K119R strain and supported by genetic and RT-Q-PCR data.

claim: The deletion of lsk1 led to an elevated level of H3 onto the ste11 promoter region.
source: Confirming our previous data, the deletion of lsk1 or the mutation of H3 lysine 14 to arginine (Htt2 K14R) led to an elevated level of H3 onto the promoter region while the htb1 K119R mutant, or a strain lacking hos2 (encoding the catalytic subunit of the SET3C HDAC) had a reduction of histone occupancy at the ste11 promoter (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The mutation of H3 lysine 14 to arginine (Htt2 K14R) led to an elevated level of H3 onto the ste11 promoter region.
source: Confirming our previous data, the deletion of lsk1 or the mutation of H3 lysine 14 to arginine (Htt2 K14R) led to an elevated level of H3 onto the promoter region while the htb1 K119R mutant, or a strain lacking hos2 (encoding the catalytic subunit of the SET3C HDAC) had a reduction of histone occupancy at the ste11 promoter (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The htb1 K119R mutant had a reduction of histone occupancy at the ste11 promoter.
source: Confirming our previous data, the deletion of lsk1 or the mutation of H3 lysine 14 to arginine (Htt2 K14R) led to an elevated level of H3 onto the promoter region while the htb1 K119R mutant, or a strain lacking hos2 (encoding the catalytic subunit of the SET3C HDAC) had a reduction of histone occupancy at the ste11 promoter (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A strain lacking hos2 (encoding the catalytic subunit of the SET3C HDAC) had a reduction of histone occupancy at the ste11 promoter.
source: Confirming our previous data, the deletion of lsk1 or the mutation of H3 lysine 14 to arginine (Htt2 K14R) led to an elevated level of H3 onto the promoter region while the htb1 K119R mutant, or a strain lacking hos2 (encoding the catalytic subunit of the SET3C HDAC) had a reduction of histone occupancy at the ste11 promoter (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The level of histone observed in the absence of ubp8 was very similar to the wild type at the ste11 promoter.
source: Importantly, the level of histone observed in the absence of ubp8 was very similar to the wild type, indicating that the upregulation of ste11 expression proceeds through a different mechanism, as already suggested above.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The upregulation of ste11 expression in the ubp8 mutant proceeds through a different mechanism than in the htb1 K119R mutant.
source: Importantly, the level of histone observed in the absence of ubp8 was very similar to the wild type, indicating that the upregulation of ste11 expression proceeds through a different mechanism, as already suggested above.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ubp8 deletion does not affect histone occupancy at the ste11 promoter.

claim: H2B ubiquitylation at the promoter of ste11 correlates with repressed transcription and high level of H3K4me3.
source: We conclude that H2B ubiquitylation at the promoter of ste11 correlates with repressed transcription and high level of H3K4me3, which in turn may favour histone deactetylation by the SET3C complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing the relationship between H2Bubi, H3K4me3, and transcriptional repression.

claim: H3K4me3 may favour histone deacetylation by the SET3C complex.
source: We conclude that H2B ubiquitylation at the promoter of ste11 correlates with repressed transcription and high level of H3K4me3, which in turn may favour histone deactetylation by the SET3C complex.
evidence: This is speculated based on the known function of SET3C and the correlation between H3K4me3 and deacetylation.

claim: The absence of either rsc1 or arp9 affected the expression of ste11.
source: The absence of either rsc1 or arp9 clearly affected the expression of ste11 while snf22 had no effect (Figure 2B), pointing to a more prominent role of RSC for ste11 expression, which was confirmed by a gametogenesis assay (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 2B and gametogenesis assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: snf22 had no effect on the expression of ste11.
source: The absence of either rsc1 or arp9 clearly affected the expression of ste11 while snf22 had no effect (Figure 2B), pointing to a more prominent role of RSC for ste11 expression, which was confirmed by a gametogenesis assay (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: RSC has a more prominent role than SWI/SNF for ste11 expression.
source: The absence of either rsc1 or arp9 clearly affected the expression of ste11 while snf22 had no effect (Figure 2B), pointing to a more prominent role of RSC for ste11 expression, which was confirmed by a gametogenesis assay (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RSC components affect ste11 expression while SWI/SNF components do not.

claim: cdc14 gene expression was affected by both the RSC and the SWI/SNF complexes.
source: In the case of cdc14, gene expression was affected by both the RSC and the SWI/SNF complexes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) as already anticipated from the identification of both rsc1 and snf22 in the LatA screen (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The SWI-SNF specific subunit Snf22 is present at the cdc14 promoter but not at the ste11 promoter.
source: The gene specificity in the requirement of either chromatin remodelers was supported by a ChIP experiment indicating that the SWI-SNF specific subunit Snf22 is present at the cdc14 promoter but not at the ste11 promoter (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The level of the Snf21 protein is strongly downregulated in the presence of ahTet.
source: Figure 2C–D shows that the level of the Snf21 protein is strongly downregulated and cell viability drops in the presence of ahTet.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2C and spot dilution assay shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Cell viability drops in the presence of ahTet in the tet0-snf21-TAP strain.
source: Figure 2C–D shows that the level of the Snf21 protein is strongly downregulated and cell viability drops in the presence of ahTet.
evidence: This is supported by spot dilution assay shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Within 3 hr of growth in the presence of ahTet, the level of both the snf21 and ste11 mRNAs was decreased by 60%.
source: Within 3 hr of growth in the presence of the drug, the level of both the snf21 and ste11 mRNAs was decreased by 60% (Figure 2E–F).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 2E–F.

claim: Within the time scale of the depletion of snf21, the level of histone H3 increased at the ste11 promoter.
source: Moreover, within the time scale of the depletion of snf21, the level of histone H3 increased at the ste11 promoter (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The catalytic subunit of RSC, Snf21, is required for ste11 expression, most likely through the displacement of nucleosomes.
source: These data indicate that the catalytic subunit of RSC, is required for ste11 expression, most likely through the displacement of nucleosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that depletion of Snf21 leads to decreased ste11 expression and increased nucleosome occupancy.

claim: The absence of arp9 resulted in a marked increased of H3 occupancy at the ste11 promoter.
source: In order to confirm this possibility, we next analyzed the level of H3 at the promoter of ste11 in a strain lacking arp9 (Figure 3A), which revealed a marked increased of H3 occupancy, reminiscent of the effect of lsk1 deletion (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Nucleosome scanning in the arp9 deleted strain and the rpb1 S2A mutant confirmed that the absence of either S2P or RSC results in higher nucleosome occupancy within the NDR of ste11.
source: Nucleosome scanning in the arp9 deleted strain and the rpb1 S2A mutant confirmed these data and provided a moderate resolution analysis of the ste11 promoter, demonstrating that the absence of either S2P or RSC results in higher nucleosome occupancy within the NDR of ste11 (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by nucleosome scanning data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The H3 acetylation promoted by S2P is required for the recruitment of RSC and subsequent nucleosome eviction at the promoter of ste11.
source: Taken together with our previous work (Materne et al., 2015), these data suggest that the H3 acetylation promoted by S2P is required for the recruitment of RSC and subsequent nucleosome eviction at the promoter of ste11.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing the relationship between S2P, H3 acetylation, RSC recruitment, and nucleosome occupancy.

claim: The abolition of either H3K14 acetylation or Lsk1 halved the occupancy of Rsc1-TAP at the ste11 promoter.
source: Supportive of this possibility, the abolition of either H3K14 acetylation or Lsk1 halved the occupancy of Rsc1-TAP at the ste11 promoter (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3C–D.

claim: The induction of ste11 was barely affected in the absence of NuA3 and NuA4 HATs.
source: We therefore tested the effect of inactivating NuA3 and NuA4 by combining a deletion of mst2, encoding the catalytic subunit of NuA3 (Gomez et al., 2005), with a ts allele of mst1, encoding the catalytic subunit of NuA3 (Gomez et al., 2008). The induction of ste11 was barely affected in the absence of these two HATs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: NuA3 and NuA4 do not participate in ste11 expression through H3K4me3.
source: This data render unlikely the possibility that NuA3 and NuA4 participate in ste11 expression through H3K4me3 and support previous data showing that Gcn5 is the primary HAT acting at the ste11 locus (Helmlinger et al., 2008).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that inactivating NuA3 and NuA4 does not affect ste11 expression.

claim: Gcn5 is the primary HAT acting at the ste11 locus.
source: This data render unlikely the possibility that NuA3 and NuA4 participate in ste11 expression through H3K4me3 and support previous data showing that Gcn5 is the primary HAT acting at the ste11 locus (Helmlinger et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: The H4K16R mutant behaved similarly to the wild type in terms of ste11 expression.
source: We also tested the effect of the H4K16R mutant (Wang et al., 2012), which behaved similarly to the wild type (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-Q-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: H2B ubiquitylation nearby the ste11 promoter impedes proper chromatin remodeling by RSC through promoter histone deacetylation by SET3C, which represses transcription.
source: Collectively, the previous experiments support that H2B ubiquitylation nearby the ste11 promoter impedes proper chromatin remodeling by RSC through promoter histone deacetylation by SET3C, which represses transcription.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: The deletion of rsc1 did not affect the level of H2B ubiquitylation nearby the ste11 promoter.
source: The deletion of rsc1 did not affect the level of H2B ubiquitylation nearby the ste11 promoter but led to a decrease of the level of this modification in the transcribed region, most likely as a consequence of decreased transcription when Rsc1 is absent (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The deletion of rsc1 led to a decrease of H2B ubiquitylation in the transcribed region of ste11.
source: The deletion of rsc1 did not affect the level of H2B ubiquitylation nearby the ste11 promoter but led to a decrease of the level of this modification in the transcribed region, most likely as a consequence of decreased transcription when Rsc1 is absent (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The decrease of H2B ubiquitylation in the transcribed region when rsc1 is deleted is most likely a consequence of decreased transcription.
source: The deletion of rsc1 did not affect the level of H2B ubiquitylation nearby the ste11 promoter but led to a decrease of the level of this modification in the transcribed region, most likely as a consequence of decreased transcription when Rsc1 is absent (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that rsc1 deletion decreases transcription and H2Bubi in the transcribed region.

claim: The abolition of either H2B ubiquitylation or histone deacetylation both resulted in a marked increase of Arp9-TAP specifically at the promoter of ste11.
source: The abolition of either H2B ubiquitylation or histone deacetylation both resulted in a marked increase of Arp9-TAP specifically at the promoter of ste11 while the absence of S2P had the opposite effect.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4B–C.

claim: The absence of S2P resulted in a decrease of Arp9-TAP at the promoter of ste11.
source: The abolition of either H2B ubiquitylation or histone deacetylation both resulted in a marked increase of Arp9-TAP specifically at the promoter of ste11 while the absence of S2P had the opposite effect.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Histone H3 acetylation was increased at the ste11 promoter when H2B ubiquitylation was abolished in either the htb1 K119R or the rhp6 mutants.
source: Moreover, histone H3 acetylation was increased at the ste11 promoter when H2B ubiquitylation was abolished in either the htb1 K119R or the rhp6 mutants (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Genome-wide mapping of nucleosome position by MNase-Seq in the rsc1 deletion mutant revealed higher occupancy upstream of the TSS.
source: In order to test if the proposed connection between the phosphorylation of serine 2 within the CTD and the RSC remodeling complex could be expanded to more genes, we performed genome-wide mapping of nucleosome position by MNase-Seq in the rsc1 deletion mutant. A meta-gene analysis of the nucleosome occupancy signal for all protein-coding genes revealed higher occupancy upstream of the TSS in the rsc1 mutant, and an average 13 bp shift of the −1 nucleosome toward the TSS was noted (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B) when selecting the 10% protein-coding genes whose promoter nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) shrinks the most in the absence of Rsc1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by MNase-Seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: An average 13 bp shift of the −1 nucleosome toward the TSS was noted in the rsc1 mutant for the 10% protein-coding genes whose promoter nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) shrinks the most.
source: A meta-gene analysis of the nucleosome occupancy signal for all protein-coding genes revealed higher occupancy upstream of the TSS in the rsc1 mutant, and an average 13 bp shift of the −1 nucleosome toward the TSS was noted (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B) when selecting the 10% protein-coding genes whose promoter nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) shrinks the most in the absence of Rsc1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by MNase-Seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: The ste11 gene belonged to the category of genes whose promoter nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) shrinks the most in the absence of Rsc1.
source: The ste11 gene belonged to that category (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), confirming the previous single gene analyses performed above.
evidence: This is supported by MNase-Seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Genes whose promoter nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) shrinks the most in the S2A mutant also showed higher nucleosome occupancy close to their TSS in the absence of Rsc1.
source: We next analysed how of the previously established list of genes whose promoter nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) shrinks the most in the S2A mutant (Materne et al., 2015) behaved when rsc1 is deleted (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D). Remarkably, these genes also showed higher nucleosome occupancy close to their TSS in the absence of Rsc1, indicating a mechanistic connection between the abolition of CTD S2P and the absence of Rsc1.
evidence: This is supported by MNase-Seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: There is a mechanistic connection between the abolition of CTD S2P and the absence of Rsc1.
source: Remarkably, these genes also showed higher nucleosome occupancy close to their TSS in the absence of Rsc1, indicating a mechanistic connection between the abolition of CTD S2P and the absence of Rsc1.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that genes affected by S2A mutation are also affected by rsc1 deletion.

claim: Comparing the subset of genes whose promoter nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) shrinks the most in the absence of either Rsc1 or in the absence of S2P revealed a significant overlap (p=3.416e-06).
source: Comparing the subset of genes whose promoter nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) shrinks the most in the absence of either Rsc1 or in the absence of S2P revealed a significant overlap (p=3.416e-06).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of MNase-Seq data.

claim: There is a genome-wide mechanistic connection between CTD phosphorylation on serine 2 and remodeling by the RSC complex.
source: These data support a genome-wide mechanistic connection between CTD phosphorylation on serine 2 and remodeling by the RSC complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the significant overlap of genes affected by S2A mutation and rsc1 deletion.

claim: The phosphorylation of the CTD S2 is not essential in yeast.
source: Despite the fact that the phosphorylation of the CTD S2 is not essential in yeast, the master regulator of gametogenesis, ste11, requires an unusual requirement of S2P nearby its promoter for proper induction to counteract the repressed state imposed by the Set1-H3K4me3-HDAC pathway (Materne et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a known fact about CTD S2 phosphorylation in yeast.

claim: ste11 requires an unusual requirement of S2P nearby its promoter for proper induction to counteract the repressed state imposed by the Set1-H3K4me3-HDAC pathway.
source: Despite the fact that the phosphorylation of the CTD S2 is not essential in yeast, the master regulator of gametogenesis, ste11, requires an unusual requirement of S2P nearby its promoter for proper induction to counteract the repressed state imposed by the Set1-H3K4me3-HDAC pathway (Materne et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: A recent study proposed that Set1 represses the transcriptome independently of H3K4 methylation and is recruited by the Atf1 transcription factor.
source: A recent study proposed that Set1 represses the transcriptome independently of H3K4 methylation and is recruited by the Atf1 transcription factor (Lorenz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Three previous studies have shown that Atf1 functions as an activator, rather than a repressor at the ste11 locus.
source: However, three previous studies have shown that Atf1 functions as an activator, rather than a repressor at the ste11 locus (Kanoh et al., 1996; Shiozaki and Russell, 1996; Takeda et al., 1995) and a H3K4R mutant also derepresses ste11 expression (Materne et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: A H3K4R mutant derepresses ste11 expression.
source: However, three previous studies have shown that Atf1 functions as an activator, rather than a repressor at the ste11 locus (Kanoh et al., 1996; Shiozaki and Russell, 1996; Takeda et al., 1995) and a H3K4R mutant also derepresses ste11 expression (Materne et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Set1 may also repress ste11 independently of its H3K4 methylase activity, but this pathway is not predominant.
source: Therefore, while we do not exclude that Set1 also represses ste11 independently of its H3K4 methylase activity, this pathway is not predominant.
evidence: This is speculated based on the evidence that H3K4R mutant derepresses ste11.

claim: A similar case to the ste11 situation (where both deletion of ubp8 and htb1 K119R result in derepression) was reported at the GAL1 locus.
source: Both the deletion of ubp8 (and therefore increased ubiquitylation) and the htb1 K119R mutant (and therefore absence of ubiquitylation) resulted in derepression of ste11. This is at first sight hard to explain as removal of histone modifications are expected to oppose the effect of their addition, such as in the acetylation/deacetylation process. However, a similar case was reported at the GAL1 locus (Henry et al., 2003), already underlying the complex dynamic of H2Bubi where the sequential addition and removal of the mark is required for proper induction.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: The sequential addition and removal of H2Bubi is required for proper induction at the GAL1 locus.
source: However, a similar case was reported at the GAL1 locus (Henry et al., 2003), already underlying the complex dynamic of H2Bubi where the sequential addition and removal of the mark is required for proper induction.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: The positive effects of the addition and removal of H2Bubi may operate through unrelated mechanisms.
source: Although the ubp8 and htb1 K119R both result in elevated ste11 expression, only the htb1 K119R suppresses the requirement of the S2 kinase Lsk1, which indicates that the positive effects of the addition and removal of the mark may operate through unrelated mechanisms.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ubp8 and htb1 K119R have different genetic interactions with lsk1.

claim: The function of lsk1 is required upstream of ubp8.
source: The fact that the double lsk1 ubp8 mutant behaves as the single lsk1 mutant suggests that the function of lsk1 is required upstream of ubp8.
evidence: This is inferred from the epistatic relationship between lsk1 and ubp8.

claim: Ubp8 positively affects elongation by facilitating the eviction of the H2A-H2B dimer and nucleosome reassembly in the wake of the polymerase.
source: Indeed if Ubp8 positively affects elongation by facilitating the eviction of the H2A-H2B dimer and nucleosome reassembly in the wake of the polymerase (Batta et al., 2011; Pavri et al., 2006), it is expected that this effect will be masked by the strong defect in polymerase occupancy at the promoter observed when lsk1 is absent.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The positive effect of ubp8 on elongation is likely to occur independently of H3K4 methylation.
source: The positive effect of ubp8 on elongation is likely to occur independently of H3K4 methylation as previously reported (Tanny et al., 2007) and maybe related to the positive role of H2Bubi in non-coding transcription at heterochromatic loci (Sadeghi et al., 2014; Zofall and Grewal, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Promoter nucleosome H2Bubi positively regulates the Set1 deposition of H3K4 methylation and therefore is the primary signal of HDAC-dependent repression of transcription.
source: The emerging model, complementing the recently propose role of S2P in ste11 induction is that promoter nucleosome H2Bubi positively regulates the Set1 deposition of H3K4 methylation and therefore is the primary signal of HDAC-dependent repression of transcription (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is the proposed model based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Upon transcriptional induction, the recruitment of SAGA-associated Ubp8 removes the ubiquitin mark.
source: Upon transcriptional induction, the recruitment of SAGA-associated Ubp8 (Helmlinger et al., 2008) removes the ubiquitin mark, and concomitantly, the MAP kinase-dependent recruitment of Lsk1 deposits higher level of S2P.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model and is supported by a citation.

claim: Upon transcriptional induction, the MAP kinase-dependent recruitment of Lsk1 deposits higher level of S2P.
source: Upon transcriptional induction, the recruitment of SAGA-associated Ubp8 (Helmlinger et al., 2008) removes the ubiquitin mark, and concomitantly, the MAP kinase-dependent recruitment of Lsk1 deposits higher level of S2P.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model.

claim: The removal of ubiquitin by Ubp8 and the deposition of S2P by Lsk1 impede the Set1-dependent recruitment and/or activation of the SET3C HDAC.
source: These two unrelated processes impede the Set1-dependent recruitment and/or activation of the SET3C HDAC, which provides access of the transcription machinery to the larger NDR that is formed.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model.

claim: The S2P-dependent induction of transcription can bypass the requirement of de-ubiquitylation dependent on Ubp8.
source: From the genetic analyses, as ste11 is highly transcribed in the ubp8 mutant, it appears that the S2P-dependent induction of transcription can bypass the requirement of de-ubiquitylation dependent on Ubp8.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ste11 is highly transcribed in the ubp8 mutant.

claim: H2B ubiquitylation was reported to act as a barrier to Ctk1 (the Lsk1 orthologue of budding yeast).
source: Considering that H2B ubiquitylation was reported to act as a barrier to Ctk1 (the Lsk1 orthologue of budding yeast) (Wyce et al., 2007), we speculate that this additional layer of control (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A) may also participate in the negative role of H2B-ub1 on ste11 induction.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: H2B ubiquitylation may also participate in the negative role of H2B-ub1 on ste11 induction by acting as a barrier to Lsk1.
source: Considering that H2B ubiquitylation was reported to act as a barrier to Ctk1 (the Lsk1 orthologue of budding yeast) (Wyce et al., 2007), we speculate that this additional layer of control (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A) may also participate in the negative role of H2B-ub1 on ste11 induction.
evidence: This is speculated based on the known function of H2Bubi in budding yeast.

claim: The level of Lsk1 was increased at the ste11 promoter when histone H2B ubiquitylation was abolished.
source: Supporting this possibility, the level of Lsk1 was increased at the ste11 promoter when histone H2B ubiquitylation was abolished (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: RSC affects the NDR of ste11 very similarly to S2P.
source: The analysis of nucleosome occupancy indicates that RSC affects the NDR of ste11 very similarly to S2P and indeed both S2P and histone acetylation are required for high occupancy of RSC at this locus.
evidence: This is inferred from the nucleosome occupancy data.

claim: Both S2P and histone acetylation are required for high occupancy of RSC at the ste11 locus.
source: The analysis of nucleosome occupancy indicates that RSC affects the NDR of ste11 very similarly to S2P and indeed both S2P and histone acetylation are required for high occupancy of RSC at this locus.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data showing reduced RSC occupancy when S2P or acetylation is reduced.

claim: RSC functions as the ultimate player required to induce ste11 transcription upon induction.
source: Considering that RSC recognizes acetylated nucleosomes through its bromodomains-containing subunits (Carey et al., 2006; Kasten et al., 2004), we propose that RSC functions as the ultimate player required to induce ste11 transcription upon induction.
evidence: This is proposed based on the known function of RSC and the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The balance between the negative effect of H2Bubi and the positive effect of RSC is critical for the timely induction of gametogenesis.
source: More specifically at the ste11 locus, the balance between the negative effect of H2Bubi and the positive effect of RSC is critical for the timely induction of gametogenesis, which highlights the major role of chromatin regulation in cell fate.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing the opposing roles of H2Bubi and RSC.

claim: Chromatin regulation plays a major role in cell fate.
source: More specifically at the ste11 locus, the balance between the negative effect of H2Bubi and the positive effect of RSC is critical for the timely induction of gametogenesis, which highlights the major role of chromatin regulation in cell fate.
evidence: This is inferred from the importance of chromatin regulation in controlling gametogenesis.
